commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[loom] Reconcile deployments through container loopback (#9391)

Apply the Loom deployment manifest through the server container's
loopback listener. The host runs the request with `docker compose exec`;
Caddy overwrites `X-Loom-Forwarded` on every public request. No
separately minted or rotated deployment token is required.

Shared mode rejects the machine-local token used by the current startup
script, leaving the new image ready while profile reconciliation returns
HTTP 401. Loom's companion change permits only an unmarked,
credential-free `deployment.reconcile` request from its own loopback
listener: https://github.com/marin-community/loom/pull/356.

The automated Loom reviewer cannot currently launch because production
federation profiles were not reconciled. Its failed check reports
`cannot mint a session credential for unauthorized user` and needs to be
rerun after the deployment is repaired. Incident record:
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/516.

---------

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[grafana] Add the async RL post-training dashboard (#9191)

Add the RL Post-training (async) dashboard for fully asynchronous
MarinSkyRL runs. It shows whether rollout work is useful and fresh and
whether it keeps the policy trainer busy: loop and buffer state,
staleness, rollout and phase timing, learner memory, ratio diagnostics
and evaluation, selected by cluster, run, training job and execution.
The existing RL dashboard becomes RL Post-training (sync), each
dashboard's run picker offers only runs of its own training loop, and
Home links each recent run to the dashboard that can select it.

Every panel reads one bounded dataset, `/v1/async-rl/overview`, which
runs nine Finelog queries per page load and serves each panel its view;
the run, job and execution pickers stay on `/query`. Each source has a
row cap and the window is capped at 7 days; a request past either cap
returns a 400 that asks the operator to narrow the selection.

Panels stay empty until a run exports the matching telemetry, and each
panel's description names the setting it needs. Each view matched the
per-panel query it replaced on two fixture stores, and the grafana suite
passes 402 tests. Display buckets start at the window start and widen on
long windows, so they can differ from other dashboards' buckets over the
same window.

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Keep MarinSkyRL external lock installable on Linux (#9390)

[Marin #9313](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9313)
already pinned SkyRL to `5b6041c5`, which contains the [compiled rollout
default](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/732). This
PR keeps that pin and fixes its external lock on Linux.

On Linux, the main-branch lock fails with:

```sh
uv sync --project config/external/MarinSkyRL --frozen --no-dev
# marin-finelog-server==0.2.55.dev35451177481 has no source distribution or Linux wheel (exit 2)
```

The [base lock
entry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/98700c7ada61aa1bdb3b1bb475110640d012f871/config/external/MarinSkyRL/uv.lock#L1136-L1141)
contains only a macOS wheel. Requiring Linux-compatible packages makes
uv select Finelog `0.2.54.dev35409391246`, which has Linux x86_64 and
aarch64 wheels. Allowing prereleases lets the external updater resolve
Marin development packages.

The same frozen sync and package imports pass after this change. The
generated pin check, 31 targeted tests, and lint also pass.
[#9360](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9360) records
the completed SkyRL activation.

Co-authored-by: Romain Yon <1596570+yonromai@users.noreply.github.com>

[rl] Use one Hydra document for SkyRL launches (#9313)

Build every SkyRL artifact as one complete Hydra launch document and
hand that document to MarinSkyRL unchanged. The same resolved
configuration drives preflight validation, Iris allocation and
submission, Ray bootstrap, task staging, training, checkpoint export,
and the persisted run manifest.

Reject topology mismatches before GPU allocation, including inconsistent
policy and rollout geometry, invalid tensor-parallel attention-head
divisibility, runtime strategy mismatches, and unequal training batches
for fully asynchronous entrypoints. Experiment choices are rendered
directly into the `skyrl` mapping instead of dotted command-line
overrides.

Move Iceball Micro, curriculum RL, and TaskTrove smoke to
artifact-producing experiment mains. Add the `launch-rl` operating skill
and a reference guide that documents the complete configuration flow and
the division between launch configuration and derived role planning.

Keep canonical portable model export independent from optional,
explicitly configured Hub publication. Pin the companion launcher after
its current-main rebase so object-store rollouts inherit distributed
RunAI loading and whole-gang startup retries.

Companion launcher change:
https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/734

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Coordinate fused CE block selection across ranks (#9368)

Coordinate fused cross-entropy block selection across the processes that
execute each kernel. Ranks compare their selection plan, cache state,
candidates, and compile viability. During JAX tracing, they choose the
first candidate that compiles on every rank, starting with the inferred
sizes. Eager callers benchmark runtime and choose the candidate with the
lowest mean across ranks. A pipeline stage coordinates only its concrete
mesh.

In the Snowball 67B SFT smoke run, ranks selected different blocks when
no shared cache key could be built; compilation then stalled in XLA's
distributed `ConfigAssigner`. The source schema now invalidates cached
winners that may have been selected by compile time. An eight-node rerun
has not validated the change.

Fixes #9038

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Skip unused tail masks in the ragged expert MLP (#9333)

Remove the three tail masks from the QuACK expert MLP on the ragged
all-to-all EP path: the forward output, the output gradient, and the
input gradient. Each mask was a full pass over the receiver buffer. The
grouped GEMMs bound their reads by the segment boundaries, and the
return transport sends only active rows, so unused rows never reach the
combine. The input-gradient tail flows only into the cotangent of the
integer-built dispatch buffer, which JAX discards. The local/FSDP expert
MLP reads its whole buffer in the combine and keeps its masks. The
transport round-trip tests now fill unused receiver capacity with NaN,
and the SM100 kernel test pads its inputs with NaN rows.

On 64 GB200 GPUs, removing the masks improves mean training throughput
by 1.76% and full-iteration throughput by 1.77%. Each arm ran three
times on the same rack, restoring the permanent hero
`2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-30000` checkpoint with the production
data mixture, batch 1024, sequence length 4096, and one process per GPU.
Each run discards 20 warmup updates and scores all 60 updates from 30020
through 30079. The control is #9366, which this PR is stacked on;
without that fix, GPU gangs launched from `main` can fail NCCL
bootstrap.

| Configuration | Mean step time | Mean iteration time | MFU | Runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Control | 14.176 s | 14.411 s | 27.69% |
[a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-control-a-20260922),
[b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-control-b-20260922),
[c](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-control-c-20260922)
|
| Tail masks removed | 13.932 s | 14.161 s | 28.18% |
[a](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-mask-a-20260922),
[b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-mask-b-20260922),
[c](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/ep-maskab-mask-c-20260922)
|

Paired gains were 2.01%, 1.62%, and 1.64%. Losses stayed finite, and the
largest matched-step loss difference from a control run was 0.00067,
against 0.00045 between control repetitions. The runs cover one rack and
exclude the hero's inter-rack collectives.

Replaces #9315. That PR also registered NCCL symmetric buffers for
all-gather and reduce-scatter; #9374 defers that change because it adds
only 0.32% on top of this one and has not been tested at hero scale
across racks or with interleaved evaluation.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
hero: rack-wide completion sampling and stable sample identity (#9387)

* hero checkpoint completions were not finishing: an unrelated hero
model change discarded every completed result, and the job needed more
wall clock than its own timeout
* sample identity no longer digests the hero model config
* `sample_id` hashed the whole `SamplingSpec`, which embedded
`draccus.encode(HERO_MODEL_CONFIG)`, so the `gpu_fa4_cute_wide` →
`gpu_fa4_cute_sm100` rename in #9332 re-keyed all 23 requests and
orphaned the 8 completed sample sets (hourly summary went 8 completed /
15 outstanding → 0 / 23) [^1]
* `SamplingSpec` now carries only the fields that decide what a sample
set contains; the architecture moves to `SampleRequest.model` as pinned
provenance
* `release` stays the deliberate backfill knob, and the checkpoint
already pins the weight layout through `metadata_digest`
* batch shape leaves the request for the same reason
* one prompt row per GPU, so the sampler reads the batch from
`jax.device_count()`; `generate` and `score_expected` take it as a
parameter
* dropless backend means filler rows cannot change another prompt's
routing, so the batch changes the pass count and not the output
* sampling moves to 64 GB200 across 16 nodes, one NVL72 rack block
* a 64-row batch covers the 46-prompt bank in one pass per sample, so a
job runs 3 decode passes instead of 6: ~4h03m → ~2h
* job `timeout` 4h → 6h
* the 4h cap sat below the measured runtime: the last two attempts died
at 4h00m during their 6th pass, and the two successes before them landed
at 3h58m
* a timeout burns one of 3 attempts, and the job keeps no partial result

[^1]: this re-keys the requests once more. the 8 earlier results stay in
the published report as a previous sampling version, and their
checkpoints get sampled again.

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fix writer and prefetch thread hangs when a producer fails (#9376)

`ThreadedBatchWriter.close()` in zephyr put its stop marker on the
bounded queue with a blocking put. If the writer thread raised after the
producer filled the queue, nothing drained the queue, so `close()` hung
and the writer's exception was never raised. `close()` now retries the
put with a timeout while the thread is alive, as `submit()` already
does, then joins and raises the stored error. This writer backs datakit
normalize and the levanter store cache, so a writer failure wedged the
shard instead of failing it.

levanter's `BackgroundIterator` producer put exception wrappers on its
bounded queue with a blocking put that ignored the stop event. If the
producer raised after `stop()` while the queue was full, the thread
blocked forever and `stop(wait=True)` (and `__del__`) hung on join.
Exceptions now go through `_enqueue`, which gives up once stop is
signaled.

Also removes two pieces of dead code: iris's `on_loop` RPC decorator and
its inline-dispatch branch in `AsyncServiceAdapter`, unused since #5988,
and marin's `with_pack` helper, whose last caller was removed in #9241.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[iris] Keep executable bits in uv task installs (#9366)

Install Iris task environments with uv's `copy` link mode instead of
`clone`. Since #9340 switched to clone mode, GPU tasks on CoreWeave have
installed wheel binaries without their executable bit: the task image's
uv 0.10.3 creates XFS reflinks with mode `0644`. The CUDA toolchain step
then found no executable `ptxas`, printed `no CUDA toolchain to stage`,
and exited before it restored CUDA 13 NCCL precedence. Pods in one gang
kept whichever of `nvidia-nccl-cu12` 2.28.9 and `nvidia-nccl-cu13`
2.31.2 uv wrote last to `nvidia/nccl/lib/libnccl.so.2`. A 64-GPU grug
run on `main` failed NCCL bootstrap with `Message truncated : received
176 bytes instead of 172`, and a second run failed the same way.

On a GB200 node, `ptxas` in `nvidia-cuda-nvcc` and in Triton kept its
mode in every link mode except clone under the image's uv:

| uv | clone | copy | hardlink | symlink |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.10.3 (task image) | `-rw-r--r--` | `-rwxr-xr-x` | `-rwxr-xr-x` |
`-rwxr-xr-x` |
| 0.11.21 | `-rwxr-xr-x` | `-rwxr-xr-x` | `-rwxr-xr-x` | `-rwxr-xr-x` |

Copy mode keeps what #9340 wanted from clone. On the node's XFS the copy
shares extents with the cache: a 4.3 GB PyTorch install added 44 MB of
used space, and the GPU environment synced in 2.98 s versus 2.99 s with
clone. A copied environment survives `uv cache clean`. Hardlink mode
falls back to a full copy with a warning for every install, because
`/uv/cache` and `/app` are separate mounts. Upgrading uv in the task
image would also fix clone mode, but the images rebuild weekly and tasks
pull `iris-task:latest`, while setup scripts ship with each job.

The toolchain step now restores cuDNN and NCCL precedence before it
looks for `ptxas`, and it fails when `ptxas` exists without the
executable bit, so this class of install damage stops setup instead of
surfacing as an NCCL bootstrap error. On a GB200 node with this branch,
setup restored both packages, staged the toolchain, and left NCCL
2.31.2+cuda13.3 on disk. The setup tests pass in a CoreWeave CPU pod,
and the new cases fail against the previous script.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Train Snowball through Levanter (#9316)

Fine-tune the Snowball Hugging Face base weights with Levanter's
registered `SnowballLMHeadModel` through the shared chat SFT launcher.
OpenThoughts Agent conversations use assistant-only loss. The recipe
keeps conversations separate because Snowball does not yet consume
Levanter's packed-document attention mask.

The 32 H100 recipe configures 32,768-token sequences with four-way
context parallelism and eight-way expert parallelism. Snowball keeps
activations split across context ranks, gathers full keys and values for
attention, and shards dense and expert weights over the context mesh.
Its scan body is checkpointed during reverse mode. On two H100s, a
bounded attention probe matched the data-sharded value and input
gradient within 1.2e-12 and 1.5e-8 after restoring execute permission on
the task-local CUDA compiler binaries. With the current Iris setup, the
same probe fails before model execution because JAX cannot execute the
installed CUDA compiler. The full 67B SFT recipe has not completed an
accelerator run; the prior 32 H100 Snowball training run (PR #9144) used
4,096-token sequences.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
Use native SM100 FA4 forward and backward kernels (#9332)

Add the `gpu_fa4_cute_sm100` attention backend, which runs upstream
FlashAttention-4 (FA4)'s native SM100 forward and backward kernels
through Marin's JAX and packed-token mask adapters, and select it in the
`moe_hero_ep` hero configuration. It supports BF16, head dimension 128,
and GQA ratios 4, 6, and 8 on SM100, and rejects other shapes and
hardware.

**Expected hero training-step throughput: about +8%** over `main`'s
`gpu_fa4_cute_wide`. This compounds the two paired studies below, each
on 64 GB200 GPUs: the native backward (+4.03%) and then the native
forward on top of it (+4.02%). No single run compared `main` with the
full change.

| Change | Result | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| Native backward vs. previous backward port | **+4.03%** training-step
throughput (15.81 → 15.19 s/step, 95% CI 1.42–6.69%) | 64 GB200, 3-pair
study stopped after interim results ([protocol and
measurements](https://github.com/mcwitt-agent/marin/tree/9cf80aafb65b1b146e9655b3f9d4346e96252ed8/experiments/benchmarks))
|
| Native forward vs. previous forward | **+4.02%** training-step
throughput (95% CI 1.11–6.92%) | [3 matched pairs, 64
GB200](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-forward-e2e-20260921d),
20 measured steps per arm, native backward in both arms |
| Forward tile 128×64 vs. default 128×128 | **2.74 → 2.10 ms** on
[packed short
documents](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-tiles-forward-20260922c),
**3.25 → 3.58 ms** on [long full-causal
documents](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-tiles-forward-20260922b)
| attention microbenchmark; 128×128 kept |

In the forward benchmark, all six runs completed 28 updates with finite
losses, and matched-step losses differed by at most 0.00031 nats. On
GB200, 18 packed-attention output and gradient parity cases pass for GQA
ratios 4, 6, and 8, with changing segment boundaries, padding, and
sliding windows ([GPU
test](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Fep-opt-d768-sm100-gqa6-parity-d-20260922)).
The training benchmarks ran on earlier revisions of the adapter code.

Context-sharded queries use #9117's layout: each shard keeps the full
K/V, the kernels apply global query offsets, and partial K/V gradients
are summed across shards.

`gpu_fa4_cute` keeps its behavior, including the H100/SM90 path, and now
shares mask, sparse-metadata, and backward pre/postprocessing code with
the new backend. The unused `gpu_fa4_cute_wide` backend is removed.

The native kernels need FA4 4.0.0b27 or newer, which `marin-core[gpu]`
and `levanter[gpu]` already require. #9353 raises the `--extra pipeline`
environment to the same versions.

commits.message:
[serve] Show per-request vLLM data in Chat (#9342)

Keep opt-in vLLM request stats on the assistant reply produced by each
model request. A collapsed Request stats block appears below Thoughts.
Tool rounds retain their own timing and token counts instead of
replacing a single last-request panel.

Stats persist with the browser's conversation history. Raw chat and
Share chat omit them. The checkbox remains off by default. Streaming
requests include token usage only while it is enabled, and timings
require `--vllm-arg=--enable-per-request-metrics` when launching the
serving job.

Chat requests also set `skip_special_tokens: false` so the response
parser receives model-native thinking and tool-call delimiters. This
matches the live Grug rollout recorded in #9343. This PR does not change
the server; #9345's CUDA fix remains separate.

The current head passed the dashboard type check, production build, and
23 Node tests.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
[grug] Add fast_track 16k dense-vs-MoE H100 scaling ladder (#9287)

Adds `experiments/grug/fast_track/` — a self-contained grug variant for
the 16k-vocab (BPE)
dense-vs-MoE comparison and MFU study on 8×H100. Rungs
d512/d768/d1024/d1280 wire the model,
optimizer, and data; the step budget data- or compute-matches each
variant's baseline (dense at
20 tokens/active-param, MoE at 60) at a per-rung batch, or is set
explicitly with `--num-steps`.
Entry point is `launch.py`; the folder README covers the ladder and
launch commands and `agent.md`
the experiment workflow.

The variant is a trimmed descendant of the moe_hero_ep grug work:
HF-config integration, the
ragged-all-to-all transport, host offload, and several always-on config
knobs were removed, and the
router-metrics telemetry was split into `router_metrics.py`, leaving
just the H100
fixed-pooled-wave-EP path.

It also lands the in-region 16k data pipeline the variant depends on:

- `experiments/datakit/shuffle_cache.py` — document-level shuffle of the
v16384 flat cache so
  sequential reads interleave domains.
- `experiments/datakit/paloma_detok.py` — byte-lossless in-region
reconstruction of the Paloma eval
  sets, avoiding the gated out-of-region download.
- `experiments/datasets/{paloma,uncheatable}.py` — eval caches gain a
tokenizer `tag` (and Paloma a
detok `raw_prefix`/`version`) so a non-llama3 tokenizer builds its own
cache instead of silently
  reusing the llama3-vocab cache and evaluating on the wrong vocab.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Guard explicit vLLM eager serving (#9345)

## Why

`--enforce-eager` disables `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs. In a
controlled Snowball Grug-67B A/B, eager decode took **44.0 ms/token**,
versus **6.52 ms/token** with vLLM's compiled default (6.75× slower).
Time to first token was 245 ms versus 83.7 ms. Compilation cost 25
seconds on the first run, and CUDA graphs used about 0.84 GiB per H100.
See #9339 for the setup, logs, and limits of this comparison.

## Changes

- Require `--i-know-i-am-making-vllm-slow` when Marin's native vLLM
server receives `--enforce-eager`. Warn about the throughput cost.
Reject `--config`/`--config=...` and abbreviated eager flags so the
guard can see the effective setting.
- Remove unproven eager settings from ten model configs, Iceball
evaluation and rollouts, and two TPU tests. [MarinSkyRL
#732](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/732) changes
the separate rollout engine's default.
- Require the promoted wheel's CUDA PyTorch build from its release
manifest. Let PyTorch select compatible NVRTC, so an incompatible CUDA
dependency fails resolution instead of selecting CPU PyTorch.

## Validation and follow-ups

- Focused server tests passed (31 on the latest commit), as did the CUDA
launcher tests and generated release pin check.
- The promoted wheel compiled, captured CUDA graphs, and served bounded
requests in
[one-H100](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fromain%2Feval-20260922-192721-sera-8b-8a47)
and
[two-H100](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fromain%2Feval-20260922-193417-sera-32b-0bc3)
smoke checks.
- [#9349](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9349) tracks
TPU validation of the changed tests.
[#9351](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9351) tracks
GB200 FlashInfer JIT validation and later CUDA install cleanup. Iceball
convergence remains unmeasured.

Fixes #9339
